questions.q: What table does a Business Rule record live on?
questions.explain: A Business Rule is a sys_script record — server-side script that runs automatically on insert, update, delete, or query.

questions.q: Which Business Rule timing type runs before the database write, and can still modify the record being saved or abort the operation entirely?
questions.explain: A before Business Rule fires before the write happens, so its field changes get included in the same save, and it can block the save outright.

questions.q: Which timing type runs after the write, in the background, non-blocking, so the user's save returns immediately?
questions.explain: Async Business Rules run after the write completes but outside the user's save transaction — the real choice for slower operations like calling an external system.

questions.q: What is a display Business Rule's real job?
options: To delete records that fail validation
To pass server-side data down to the client when the form loads, before the page renders
To run only on scheduled Import Sets
To replace the need for a UI Policy entirely
questions.explain: Display Business Rules run at form load time specifically to get server-side data to the client for the form's client scripts to use.

questions.q: Why are Business Rules considered more powerful, and riskier, than UI Policies or Data Policies?
options: They are actually less powerful, since they can only touch one field
They can read or write any field on any record, cascade changes across unrelated tables, and have no built-in boundary the way field-level policies do
They only run once per ServiceNow instance, ever
They cannot be scoped to a specific table
questions.explain: Unlike a UI or Data Policy's narrow field-level scope, a Business Rule's script has essentially no limit on what it can touch, which is exactly why a poorly scoped one is risky.
